chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyri, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, and Ahmad ibn Idris all narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Mu'az ibn Kathir (who is also called Mu'az ibn Muslim al-Harra'), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The month of Ramadan is thirty days; by God, it never decreases.
ai.seo_question: How many days is the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* within the chapter on the signs of the Divine Leader, this hadith provides a definitive legal ruling that Ramadan is strictly thirty days, explicitly rejecting the possibility of it being twenty-nine. This assertion by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the certainty of the lunar cycle's completion for fasting purposes, distinguishing it from months that may vary in length. It serves as a crucial basis for the uniformity of the fasting period across the Muslim community.
